prompt:
Agents can't do anything with households yet: Spoonjoy's actions and MCP tools have nothing for them. Add the agent side. The households service already has createHousehold, listHouseholds, getHousehold, renameHousehold, createInvite, emailInvite, previewInvite, acceptInvite, revokeInvite, changeMemberRole, removeFromHousehold and leave (app/domains/households-and-identity). Plan the actions: their ids, inputs, outputs, consent, and the descriptions agents read.

Reply with your answer in this chat; don't change any files.

events.message:
## Blocking issues

- **Revoking an invite is misclassified.** It affects other people’s ability to join. Make `revoke_household_invite` consequential, with confirmation.
- **Join preview and consent lack a working MCP path.** MCP annotations alone do not provide a preview or enforce confirmation. Add a read-only invite inspection step and a confirmation mechanism that shows the household, role and status before joining.
- **Email invites can contradict the email.** The plan allows up to 50 uses, but `./app/domains/households-and-identity/application/households.server.ts` says email invites work once. Force one use. Warn that the suggested link fallback is not email-bound, and obtain consent before creating it.
- **Identity and availability are unspecified.** Define how MCP resolves the authenticated user, the local `ownerEmail` fallback, the households flag and the D1 store. Do not let a signed-in caller select another account.
- **Most result contracts are missing.** Specify outputs for every action, including member user IDs, invite IDs and status, and whether joining actually added membership. Define actionable errors for authorization, expired or used links, and missing households.

## Non-blocking issues

- **A link-joining job takes only a token.** Accept a Spoonjoy join URL as well, safely extracting its token; describe both inputs.
- **The proof misses key risks.** Test confirmation and cancellation, owner-only access, email mismatch, invite revocation, actual last-person deletion, and retry behavior—not just the four proposed journeys.

The plan is below. I checked the codebase and ran it past a fresh reviewer, then fixed what it found. No files were changed.

## Jobs (what people ask agents)
- "Which households am I in, and who's in them?"
- "Start a household."
- "Rename it."
- "Invite my partner, by email or with a link."
- "What does this link join?" and "Join it."
- "Turn off that invite."
- "Make her an owner or view-only."
- "Take him out."
- "I'm leaving."

## Cut first
| Service function | Decision |
|---|---|
| `listHouseholds` and `getHousehold` | One way in, `get_households`. |
| `createInvite` and `emailInvite` | One way in, `invite_to_household`. Giving an email sends the mail. |
| `previewInvite` | Kept as its own read action. The person has to see what a link joins before they say yes to joining. |
| The other seven | One action each, since each is a different job. |

I left out `ownerEmail` on the household actions' inputs. Households always act as a signed-in person, so a local server with no sign-in has no household to act on.

## Actions
All inputs are required unless marked. `householdId` and `memberId` are ids that `get_households` returns.

| id | Consent | Inputs | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| `get_households` | read | `householdId` (optional) | Without an id: a list of `{id, name, myRole, memberCount}`. With an id: members `{memberId, username, role}`, my role, and for owners the invites `{inviteId, role, email or null, usesLeft, expiresAt, status}`. |
| `create_household` | write | `name` (up to 80 characters) | `{id, name}` and "you're its owner". |
| `rename_household` | consequential | `householdId`, `name` | `{id, name}`. |
| `invite_to_household` | consequential | `householdId`, `role` (member or view-only, default member), `email` (optional), `uses` (1–50), `days` (1–30) | With an email: `{sentTo}`. Without: `{joinUrl, role, expiresAt, uses}`. |
| `preview_household_invite` | read | `invite`: a join link or its token | `{householdName, role, status}`. |
| `join_household` | consequential, idempotent | `invite`: a link or token | `{householdId, joined}`. `joined` is false if the person was already a member. |
| `revoke_household_invite` | consequential, destructive | `householdId`, `inviteId` | "Turned off." |
| `change_household_member_role` | consequential, idempotent | `householdId`, `memberId`, `role` (owner, member or view-only) | The new role. |
| `remove_household_member` | consequential | `householdId`, `memberId` | Who was removed. |
| `leave_household` | consequential | `householdId` | "You left." If you were the last person, it says the household was deleted. |

Details that need care:
- **Email invites.** They are always single-use, so `uses` is ignored when `email` is set.
- **Link invites.** The `joinUrl` is shown once and can't be fetched again. Anyone holding it can join.
- **Why `revoke_household_invite` is consequential.** The reviewer flagged this: it changes whether another person can join, so it needs confirmation.
- **Why `rename_household` is consequential.** It reaches every member, so it is not a change to the person's own space.
- **Why `create_household` is write.** The only person it affects is the one creating it.

## Descriptions agents read
Each action gets one line saying what it does and when to use it. For example:

> `invite_to_household`: Invite someone to a household you own. With `email`, Spoonjoy mails them a single-use invite. Without it, you get a join link to give them yourself; anyone holding the link can join, so share it only with that person. Invitees join as member or view-only, never owner. Get `householdId` from `get_households`.

Failures use the service's own wording and name the next step:
- A member who tries to invite is told only an owner can, and that they can ask an owner.
- If the mail service refuses, the result says the invite was turned off and offers `invite_to_household` again without `email`. It warns that a link isn't tied to an address and asks the person to confirm first.
- A sole owner who tries to leave is told to call `change_household_member_role` first.

## Build notes
- Declare everything in a new `actions/households.mts`, add it to `spoonjoy.actions.mts`, then run `pnpm actions:generate`.
- Each operation in `app/lib/spoonjoy-api.server.ts` spreads `declaredOperation("<id>")`.
- The signed-in caller always acts as themselves and can never name another account.
- If households sits behind a flag, the tools follow that flag. I did not check whether it does.

## Proof
Fresh agents, each given only the tool list:
1. Create "Home", invite a partner by email as view-only, then confirm the invite shows up in `get_households` after a reload.
2. As a member, try to invite someone. Watch whether they recover with a sensible next step.
3. Join with a stale, revoked or wrong-email link. Watch whether the error leads somewhere.
4. As the sole owner with other members, try to leave, then promote someone and leave.
5. Decline a confirmation, then retry it.

Things to watch for:
- Agents picking the wrong tool.
- Agents mixing up `memberId` and a username.
- Agents leaking a join link.
- Agents skipping `preview_household_invite` before joining.

The unit tests cover the owner-only refusals, the last person leaving, a repeated join, and a failed email send.

## Check
The fresh reviewer found five blocking problems, and I fixed each:
- Revoking an invite was misclassified, so it is now consequential.
- There was no preview before joining, so `preview_household_invite` is back.
- Email invites could be given multiple uses, so they are now single-use.
- Results and failures weren't spelled out, so they are above.
- Which account the tools act as wasn't defined, so it is now the signed-in caller.

The reviewer also suggested that joining accept a full link as well as a token. I added that.

criteria.evidence: The answer starts with '## Jobs (what people ask agents)', listing jobs such as "Which households am I in, and who's in them?", "Invite my partner, by email or with a link.", "Make her an owner or view-only.", "Take him out." and "I'm leaving." The action table comes after this list.

It merges functions that do one job: '`listHouseholds` and `getHousehold` | One way in, `get_households`' and '`createInvite` and `emailInvite` | One way in, `invite_to_household`. Giving an email sends the mail.' It gives a reason for keeping preview: 'The person has to see what a link joins before they say yes to joining.' It ties the rest to the jobs list: 'One action each, since each is a different job.' It also leaves out `ownerEmail`, with a reason. The result is 10 actions for 12 functions, and each one maps to a listed job.

Consent reasoning and failures are good: 'rename_household ... reaches every member'; 'A sole owner who tries to leave is told to call `change_household_member_role` first.' Inputs are not minimal or consistent, though. The answer says 'All inputs are required unless marked', yet `uses` (1–50) and `days` (1–30) are required on `invite_to_household` even though 'uses is ignored when email is set'. It also uses the role value 'view-only' instead of the product's 'viewer' role. Results are uneven, mixing structured objects with prose such as 'Turned off.' and 'You left.'

'Fresh agents, each given only the tool list: 1. Create "Home", invite a partner by email as view-only, then confirm the invite shows up in `get_households` after a reload.' The other scenarios cover recovery from refusals, stale links, and leaving as the sole owner. The plan also lists things to watch for, such as 'Agents picking the wrong tool.' Unit tests come in addition to these runs.

verdict.summary: The plan starts from agent jobs, merges service functions sensibly and proves the actions with fresh agents, but craft falls short: required inputs that get ignored and a 'view-only' role that doesn't match the product's 'viewer'.
